summary: Raiders named 15th-year veteran Kirk Cousins the Week 1 starting QB over rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza and incumbent Aidan O'Connell, per HC Klint Kubiak ("Kirk's had a really good offseason, very good camp and he's earned it"). Gives Bowers a proven, accurate veteran passer (76.5% completion in preseason) rather than a rookie learning on the job to open the season.

Trending toward playing Week 1 against the Rams in Melbourne after two positive practice days and making the 15-hour flight to Australia; activated off PUP in late August following his January Achilles tear. Per Ian Rapoport, no setback reported, though the club has not confirmed he'll see a full workload this soon post-surgery.

Survived the August ankle scare and made Carolina's 53-man roster, one of five TEs kept (with Tremble, Evans, Franks, and new addition Darren Waller). Despite that, GM Dan Morgan confirmed Sanders is drawing outside trade interest; Morgan says the team is "committed" to him for now but left the door open ("not to say that something couldn't change"). Snaps in this room will be split five ways.

Still being eased into Carolina's offense in a slow ramp-up after his mid-August signing; took only limited/side-work reps in Monday's practice rather than full team drills. A clean Week 1 workload isn't assured yet, even though the team plans to feature him once he's fully up to speed in Dave Canales' scheme.

Remains an unsigned free agent as of Aug. 31, nine months out from his December 2025 ACL tear; report describes him "trending towards" a reunion with the Eagles, whose interest reportedly stems from the slow development of 2nd-round rookie TE Eli Stowers. Nothing imminent per the report — his 2026 team is still unresolved this close to Week 1.

The Rams' first official Week 1 depth chart lists two co-starter pairings rather than a hierarchy: Tyler Higbee/Davis Allen at one spot, Parkinson/Terrance Ferguson at the other, with rookie Max Klare fifth. Beat coverage expects Parkinson, Higbee, and Ferguson to see the most snaps in a heavy rotation — confirms the four-way committee is real and now has its specific pairings, not just a vague "nobody separates" forecast.

Will begin the season on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list with a neck injury, per the Packers' own site — removes him from Week 1 availability entirely and pushed Green Bay to sign veteran Jonnu Smith and trade for Mark Redman as insurance behind Tucker Kraft.

With Luke Musgrave opening the year on PUP (neck), Smith is set for a clearer complementary pass-catching role behind starter Tucker Kraft than a straight camp-battle add would suggest; he cited real familiarity with HC Matt LaFleur's system from their 2017 overlap in Tennessee ("at most, three years of his career outside the framework of this offense"). Green Bay also traded a 2028 7th-rounder to the Rams for blocking TE Mark Redman to round out the room.

Entering Week 1 without a settled role in a genuine three-way Chargers TE rotation — the team's own unofficial depth chart lists Kolar/Gadsden/Njoku with "OR" between all three names. Beat coverage frames Kolar as the blocking-first TE1 and Gadsden as the receiving threat who could grow his snap share at Njoku's expense if he improves as a blocker; Njoku himself "must prove himself early" to secure meaningful snaps under new OC Mike McDaniel. A muddier three-way picture than the clean Njoku-ahead-of-Gadsden hierarchy reported in late August.

Led the Jets in receptions in 2025 (44 on 65 targets) before a season-ending neck injury and remains the room's clear top pass-catcher, but new OC Frank Reich isn't naming a single lead TE — he described the roster as having "like 15" starters and said he plans to play the whole TE room, with Jeremy Ruckert also in the mix. Not the clean "Sadiq takes over as TE1" outcome some late-August coverage projected.

Back at position drills Sept. 1 for the first time in nearly a month after his hernia-surgery setback, and HC Aaron Glenn says he's on track for Week 1 — but explicitly not for a full workload: Glenn said the plan is to build him to a managed snap count ("20, 25, or another amount"), not to guarantee "60 plays." A limited-role Week 1 debut, not the unrestricted starter some outlets have projected.

Fully back at practice Sept. 1 after the abductor/groin strain that sidelined him in mid-to-late August; by all reports operating with no restrictions heading into the Sept. 13 opener against Baltimore. Resolves the injury scare cleanly in his favor after a Pro Bowl rookie year (76-817-4).
